title: Tonight, not tomorrow
setting: Early evening at the office. Yuki and Mai are about to go out for dinner when they hear thunder the forecast never mentioned.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: ね、マイ、今日ご飯行かない？
lines.kana: ね、まい、きょうごはんいかない？
lines.english: Hey, Mai, want to go out for dinner tonight?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ii ne, iku iku! are? ima, kaminari natta?
lines.ja: いいね、行く行く！あれ？今、雷鳴った？
lines.kana: いいね、いくいく！あれ？いま、かみなりなった？
lines.english: Sounds good, I'm in! Huh? Was that thunder just now?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, uso. kyou wa ame furanai tte, tenki yohou de itteta yo.
lines.ja: え、うそ。今日は雨降らないって、天気予報で言ってたよ。
lines.kana: え、うそ。きょうはあめふらないって、てんきよほうでいってたよ。
lines.english: What, no way. The forecast said it wasn't going to rain today.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: demo, kiite. honto ni kaminari natteru yo.
lines.ja: でも、聞いて。ほんとに雷鳴ってるよ。
lines.kana: でも、きいて。ほんとにかみなりなってるよ。
lines.english: But listen. It really is thundering.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: aa, honto da. tenki yohou, mata hazureta ne.
lines.ja: ああ、ほんとだ。天気予報、また外れたね。
lines.kana: ああ、ほんとだ。てんきよほう、またはずれたね。
lines.english: Oh, you're right. The forecast got it wrong again.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ne, taifuu kuru no, ashita ja nakatta?
lines.ja: ね、台風来るの、明日じゃなかった？
lines.kana: ね、たいふうくるの、あしたじゃなかった？
lines.english: Hey, wasn't the typhoon supposed to come tomorrow?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sou da yo ne. chotto mite miru. e! taifuu, konban kuru tte!
lines.ja: そうだよね。ちょっと見てみる。え！台風、今晩来るって！
lines.kana: そうだよね。ちょっとみてみる。え！たいふう、こんばんくるって！
lines.english: I thought so. Let me check. What?! It says the typhoon's coming tonight!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, konban? tenki yohou, hazurete bakkari!
lines.ja: え、今晩？天気予報、外れてばっかり！
lines.kana: え、こんばん？てんきよほう、はずれてばっかり！
lines.english: Tonight? That forecast is always wrong!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: da yo ne! are? chotto yuretenai?
lines.ja: だよね！あれ？ちょっと揺れてない？
lines.kana: だよね！あれ？ちょっとゆれてない？
lines.english: Tell me about it! Huh? Isn't it shaking a little?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: bikkuri shita. ima no jishin, doko de okita no kana.
lines.ja: びっくりした。今の地震、どこで起きたのかな。
lines.kana: びっくりした。いまのじしん、どこでおきたのかな。
lines.english: That gave me a fright. I wonder where that earthquake was.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: chiba de okita tte. ookii jishin ja nakute yokatta.
lines.ja: 千葉で起きたって。大きい地震じゃなくてよかった。
lines.kana: ちばでおきたって。おおきいじしんじゃなくてよかった。
lines.english: It says it was in Chiba. Good thing it wasn't a big one.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: taifuu wa kuru shi, kaminari wa natteru shi, jishin mo okita shi. kyou, nan na no?
lines.ja: 台風は来るし、雷は鳴ってるし、地震も起きたし。今日、何なの？
lines.kana: たいふうはくるし、かみなりはなってるし、じしんもおきたし。きょう、なんなの？
lines.english: A typhoon's on its way, it's thundering, and now an earthquake. What is with today?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: gomen, yuki. kyou wa mou uchi kaette ii? neko ga kaminari nigate na no.
lines.ja: ごめん、ユキ。今日はもううち帰っていい？猫が雷苦手なの。
lines.kana: ごめん、ゆき。きょうはもううちかえっていい？ねこがかみなりにがてなの。
lines.english: Sorry, Yuki. Would it be okay if I just went home today? My cat's scared of thunder.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ii yo, ii yo. gohan wa raishuu ne.
lines.ja: いいよ、いいよ。ご飯は来週ね。
lines.kana: いいよ、いいよ。ごはんはらいしゅうね。
lines.english: Of course, go. We'll do dinner next week.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: arigatou. kondo wa tenki yohou, hazurete hoshii naa.
lines.ja: ありがとう。今度は天気予報、外れてほしいなあ。
lines.kana: ありがとう。こんどはてんきよほう、はずれてほしいなあ。
lines.english: Thanks. This time I'm hoping the forecast is wrong.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un. demo, sou iu yohou wa ataru n da yo ne.
lines.ja: うん。でも、そういう予報は当たるんだよね。
lines.kana: うん。でも、そういうよほうはあたるんだよね。
lines.english: Yeah. But those are always the ones that turn out right.

choices.english: The typhoon is due tomorrow, as forecast, so they go to dinner tonight before it arrives.
Dinner is called off: the typhoon turns out to be coming tonight, not tomorrow, there's a small earthquake, and Mai heads home to her cat, who's scared of thunder.
A big earthquake hits Chiba, so Yuki and Mai stay late at the office together until it's safe.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Yuki suggests dinner and Mai says yes (line 2). Then they hear thunder (lines 2 and 4), though the forecast said no rain (line 3). Line 7: the news says the typhoon is coming tonight, not tomorrow (taifuu, konban kuru tte!). Lines 9-12: a small earthquake (ookii jishin ja nakute yokatta). Lines 14-15: Mai asks to go home because her cat is scared of thunder, and Yuki moves dinner to next week (gohan wa raishuu ne). A is wrong: the forecast said tomorrow, but the news says tonight (lines 6-8), and dinner is off. C is wrong: the quake in Chiba wasn't a big one (line 12), and Mai goes home rather than staying.

questions.english: Mai asks you, "ne, ashita, kaimono ikanai?" (Want to go shopping tomorrow?) You've heard a typhoon is coming tomorrow. Tell her.
questions.ja: ね、明日、買い物行かない？
questions.kana: ね、あした、かいものいかない？
questions.answer: Say a typhoon is coming tomorrow, with taifuu and kuru: demo, ashita taifuu kuru yo.

modelAnswers.english: But there's a typhoon coming tomorrow.

modelAnswers.romaji: ashita wa taifuu ga kuru tte.
modelAnswers.ja: 明日は台風が来るって。
modelAnswers.english: They say a typhoon's coming tomorrow.

questions.explanation: A typhoon comes: kuru. English 'a typhoon hits' pushes you to utsu or ataru, which don't work with the typhoon as the subject. The scene uses the same pair in line 6 (taifuu kuru no, ashita ja nakatta?) and line 7 (taifuu, konban kuru tte!). The second answer adds tte, 'they say', the way Yuki passes on the news in line 7. Ataru only works the other way round, with your plans as the subject: ryokou ga taifuu ni atatchatta (our trip ran into a typhoon).

questions.english: Once the shaking is over, Yuki wonders about the earthquake. What does she say?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、地震のあと何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、じしんのあとなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, jishin no ato nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I wonder where that earthquake rang out.
choices.romaji: ima no jishin, doko de natta no kana.

choices.english: I wonder where that earthquake struck.
choices.romaji: ima no jishin, doko o utta no kana.

choices.english: I wonder where that earthquake happened.
choices.romaji: ima no jishin, doko de okita no kana.

questions.explanation: Line 11: Yuki says ima no jishin, doko de okita no kana, and Mai answers with the same verb in line 12 (chiba de okita tte). An earthquake happens: okiru. A uses naru, the verb thunder takes (line 4: kaminari natteru); an earthquake doesn't ring. B is English 'strike' or 'hit' put into Japanese: utsu is hitting with a hand or a bat, and an earthquake never utsu. While it shakes, people just shout jishin da!, as Mai does in line 10. Yuki lines up all three verbs in line 13: taifuu wa kuru, kaminari wa natteru, jishin mo okita.

questions.english: Yuki doubts there's any thunder, because the forecast said no rain. Mai answers, "demo, kiite. honto ni kaminari natteru yo." What can she hear?
questions.ja: マイさんは、何が聞こえましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、なにがきこえましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, nani ga kikoemashita ka?

choices.english: Thunder: it's rumbling outside right now.
Nothing yet: the sky is turning stormy, and thunder is on its way.
A bolt of lightning that has just hit something near the office.

questions.explanation: Line 4: kaminari natteru is naru 鳴る, 'make a sound', the verb a phone or an alarm takes, in its -teru form: thunder is rumbling right now. In line 2 Mai heard one clap (ima, kaminari natta?), and by line 4 it's still going. B mixes it up with naru 'become': the two sound alike, but 'ring' is said flat (na-RU) while 'become' falls (NA-ru), and nobody says the weather is turning into thunder. C would be kaminari ga ochita (lightning struck); nothing in the scene was hit.

questions.english: Mai looks out at a dry street and says, "kyou, ame furu tte itteta noni, furanakatta ne." (They said it would rain today, but it didn't.) Agree, and grumble that the forecast got it wrong.
questions.ja: 今日、雨降るって言ってたのに、降らなかったね。
questions.kana: きょう、あめふるっていってたのに、ふらなかったね。
questions.romaji: kyou, ame furu tte itteta noni, furanakatta ne.
questions.answer: Say the forecast missed, with tenki yohou and hazureru in the past: un, tenki yohou hazureta ne.

modelAnswers.ja: うん、天気予報外れたね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, the forecast got it wrong.

modelAnswers.ja: 天気予報、また外れたよ。

questions.explanation: A forecast misses (hazureru) or hits (ataru), like a guess. As a grumble it's almost always past, hazureta, as Yuki says in line 5 (tenki yohou, mata hazureta ne); Mai's hazurete bakkari in line 8 means it keeps getting things wrong. Not machigaeru: that's a person making a slip, so yohou ga machigaeta doesn't work. The opposite comes at the end: Mai hopes the typhoon forecast is wrong this time (line 16: hazurete hoshii naa), and Yuki says those are the ones that turn out right (line 17: sou iu yohou wa ataru n da yo ne).

newWords.english: again (mata hazureta = got it wrong again)
Chiba, the prefecture just east of Tokyo
be right, hit the mark (a forecast, a guess); the opposite of hazureru
